transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve barely been sleeping since the warehouse inspection. I just lie there replaying pieces of it, and if I do fall asleep, I wake up sweating and wide awake, like I’m back near that blast again.
Do you ever feel like you’re reliving the warehouse inspection during the day, like having flashbacks or vivid memories that come out of nowhere?

Yes. It happens during the day, even when I’m trying to focus on work. I’ll be reviewing a policy or reading a loss report, and suddenly I get this really sharp image of the worker on the floor, and the soot in the air. It comes out of nowhere, and my body reacts before I can really stop it.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of the warehouse inspection or what happened there?

Yes. I’ve been avoiding the warehouse file, honestly. Even opening emails about it makes my stomach drop, so I keep putting it off. And if calls come in about industrial accounts, I’ve been letting them go to voicemail instead of picking up.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms, including intrusive memories, flashbacks, avoidance of reminders, and physiological reactivity to trauma-related stimuli, are consistent with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Other candidates like F41.1 (Panic Disorder), F41.9 (Anxiety Disorder, Unspecified), and G47.00 (Insomnia, Unspecified) are ruled out as the symptoms are specifically tied to a traumatic event and meet full criteria for F43.10. No further questioning is needed.
